title: Model routing by assessed complexity
summary: Operator ask 2026-09-14: the regular-expression approach to complexity is nonsense; the workflow should be work order → analysis → implementation plan → implementation, with analysis and plan as pipeline steps that declare complexity, and Token Economy as the measuring authority owning the estimation prompts, the calibration study, and the versioned (complexity class → model, thinking level) pair table, fed by a reported-versus-achieved record from every closed card. Current picture verified against v0.3.0: three regexes over title+prompt in ModelRoutingPolicyRegistry, no analysis or plan pipeline step, claude-fable-5-1 unreachable, claude-opus-5 reachable only through the critical-floor keyword list, and no record joining a routed (model, level) pair to its outcome. Research reviewed: routing/cascade literature treats difficulty as a prediction checked against outcome, LLM-as-judge literature requires measured calibration rather than assumed reliability, and code-task difficulty prediction requires fitting and checking a rubric against this product's own history before trusting it. Three alternatives compared (report-only, two new pipeline steps with Token Economy owning the pair table, single external Token Economy call); Option B recommended. Five open decisions: analysis/plan scope, requalification authority, pair-table ownership, evidence bar before the table changes, and the disagreement protocol.

review.note: The proposed complexity workflow remains open: develop still qualifies intake with three regular-expression signals and has no analysis, plan, requalification, or complexity-outcome loop, although AGT-2811 has added thinking level to token telemetry.
